note: Synthetic examples. No real client data.

input.brief: Our three-hospital network has emergency department wait times averaging 4.6 hours, well above the state median of 2.9 hours. Patient satisfaction scores dropped 12 points this year and two payers have raised concerns. The board wants a plan within one quarter that does not require new construction. Nursing staff are already stretched.

problem_statement.summary: Lakeside Health's emergency departments average 4.6-hour waits versus a 2.9-hour state median, contributing to a 12-point satisfaction drop and payer concern.
problem_statement.key_question: How can Lakeside Health reduce ED wait times toward the state median within 12 months without new construction or added strain on nursing staff?
business_objectives: Reduce average ED wait time toward the state median

missing_information.item: Hourly arrival and boarding data by site
Payer contract terms tied to quality metrics

assumptions: Wait time is measured door-to-provider consistently across sites

input.brief: We sell accounting software to small firms. Net revenue retention fell from 112% to 96% over 18 months. Sales says the product lacks features; product says sales oversells to the wrong customers; customer success says onboarding is understaffed. We need to know what is really driving churn and what to fix first, ahead of a fundraising round in nine months. Engineering capacity is fixed for the next two quarters.

problem_statement.summary: Ledgerly's net revenue retention fell from 112% to 96% in 18 months, with internal teams offering conflicting explanations (feature gaps, poor-fit customers, under-resourced onboarding).
problem_statement.key_question: Which drivers explain Ledgerly's retention decline, and which fixes will most improve net revenue retention before the fundraising round in nine months, given fixed engineering capacity?
business_objectives: Identify root causes of churn and contraction
Present a credible retention story to investors
constraints: Engineering capacity fixed for two quarters

in_scope: Churn driver analysis by cohort and segment

missing_information.item: Customer-level churn and contraction data with acquisition source
Churn reason codes or exit survey results

assumptions: Conflicting internal explanations are hypotheses to test, not established facts

input.brief: We want to use AI to grow the business. What should we do?

missing_information.item: Definition of growth (revenue, margin, customers, markets)
Budget, timeline and existing data or technology assets

clarifying_questions: What does your business sell, to whom, and roughly how large is it?
What kind of growth matters most: revenue, profitability, new customers, or new markets? Is there a target?
What budget and timeline are you working with, and what customer or operational data do you already collect?
Is there a specific problem (for example slow sales cycles or high support costs) that prompted this question?
